text:
alina (support): flagging a high-severity customer escalation — multiple customers reporting huge p95/p99 spikes since ~08:10 UTC. Support page shows 20% error rate for /v1/generate in the hosted cluster. Customers: org-42, org-77. Tickets linked: <https://zendesk/issue/4321>.

sam (oncall): thanks alina — I'm on it. Can you paste example request IDs or trace ids? Any pattern on model, region, or route?

alina (support): sample trace ids: trace:ab12cd34, trace:ef56gh78. Most are `model: redwood-large-v2` and `region: us-east-1`. Payload sizes normal (avg 512 tokens). Several reports say p95 from 220ms -> 1.8s, p99 up to 5s. No auth or billing errors.

lee (eng-runtime): seeing the same in Grafana. p95 for redwood-large-v2 in us-east-1 jumped ~8x at 08:09 UTC. CPU on inference hosts OK but GPU utilization dropped on a subset of pods (waiting on KV cache). Traces show long stall in KV cache lookup + node-local disk I/O. Logs for a sample request: 

```
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z INFO request_id=trace:ab12cd34 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-large-v2 step=kv_cache_lookup latency_ms=1200 node=inf-12
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z WARN request_id=trace:ab12cd34 node=inf-12 disk_io_ms=1150 kernel=io_wait
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z ERROR request_id=trace:ab12cd34 fallback=none reason=kv_timeout
```

lee (eng-runtime): looks like a transient regression in our local KV store backend (rocksdb compaction/GC) that increased local disk latency on a small subset of nodes. That's causing tail latency spikes for requests hitting those nodes. The routing still sends requests round-robin, so p99 overall increases.

chris (eng-sre): good find. Immediate mitigations we can flip (low-risk):
- enable route-level circuit breaker to evade nodes with high disk_iowait (threshold: 500ms).
- add a temporary fallback routing policy for `redwood-large-v2` to prefer hosts with healthy KV latency.
- enable model fallback to `redwood-large-v2-quant-small` for non-SLA customers (to reduce tail latency).
- increase read cache TTL to reduce KV hits for repeated prefixes.

chris (eng-sre): example admin API call to enable the circuit breaker for the route (run from backstage/admin box):

```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routes/circuit-breaker" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","metric":"kv_lookup_ms","threshold":500,"action":"route_away"}'
```

sam (oncall): I'll roll that now and watch metrics. Also will scale a small burst pool and change routing to prefer us-west-2 for a minute if us-east p99 stays high. @lee can you confirm no ongoing deploys?\
lee (eng-runtime): no deploys at 08:00-08:20. There's a maintenance compaction job scheduled for that cluster window — it should have been throttled but looks like compaction ran harder than expected on hosts inf-11/12/13. I'm pausing the compaction scheduler for that shard.

deploy-bot: compaction-scheduler pause requested by @lee. job_id=comp-2026-03-15-0810. status=queued -> running -> paused.

maria (product): what's customer impact and timeframe? If we route to fallback models, any change in output quality we should proactively communicate?

chris (eng-sre): immediate customer impact: transient latency increase for ~5% of requests hitting affected nodes. Rolling circuit-breaker and routing away reduces p99 by half in my local canary (simulated). Fallback to quantized model reduces latency but could slightly change logits; recommend opt-in per org (non-SLA) or automatic for non-critical routes. We should draft a brief status message for customers if >5% calls affected.

sam (oncall): actions I'm taking now:
1) POST circuit-breaker via admin API (see above).
2) Update routing policy to prefer hosts with kv_lookup_ms < 200ms.
3) Open temporary region failover rule (route weight us-east-1:60%, us-west-2:40%) for redwood-large-v2 for 30m.
4) Throttle background compactions on affected shard.

sam (oncall): running circuit-breaker...

```
# run result
{"status":"ok","changes":[{"route":"/v1/generate","cb_set":true,"threshold_ms":500}]}
```

sam (oncall): routing policy updated. watch grafana p95/p99 panels.

lee (eng-runtime): verified compaction paused on inf-11/12/13. KV tail latency dropping on those nodes. Traces now show kv_lookup_ms back to ~60ms for recent requests.

chris (eng-sre): to prevent recurrence, follow-up engineering work:
- add reactive node health tagging based on kv_lookup_ms and disk_iowait (auto-evict if >3 failures in 5m).
- improve compaction throttling and add guardrail to stop heavy compaction if disk_iowait > 300ms.
- add a canary that exercises KV under load after compaction schedule changes.

alina (support): customers updated: sent short note to org-42 and org-77 explaining latency spike and mitigation.

maria (product): please prepare a 1-sentence status we can put in status.redwood.com if this affects >10% of customers within next hour.

sam (oncall): current telemetry after mitigations (08:18 UTC): p95 redwood-large-v2 us-east-1 = 280ms (was 1.8s), p99 = 650ms (was 5s). Error rate down to 0.8% (was 20%). I'll keep this thread updated.

lee (eng-runtime): repro steps for devs to recreate tail while we test fixes:
1) run load test against single node: `ab -n 2000 -c 50 -p small_request.json http://inf-12.local/v1/generate`
2) trigger compaction stress: `admin-tool compaction --shard=s-12 --intensity=100` (only in staging)
3) watch `kv_lookup_ms` in metrics and trace slow requests via `trace:...` header.

chris (eng-sre): SLO guardrail checklist to create as follow-up ticket:
- default route-level circuit breaker config (thresholds for kv/disk/exec).
- tenant concurrency limits and token-per-second rate limits per org tier.
- automatic fallback model policy (non-SLA only) + notification hooks.
- region failover policy with graceful weight shift and autoscaling budget.

sam (oncall): ticket created: ENG-SRE-7123 tracking guardrails + postmortem. Assigning to @chris and @lee for fixes.

alina (support): closing loop with customers; will reopen if they see anomalies. thanks team :thumbsup:

sam (oncall): monitoring for 30m, will escalate to incident channel if metrics regress.

(End of thread)
